edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: The Mediterranean pattern combines unsaturated fats, fiber-rich plant foods, and lower ultra-processed intake, which together improve lipids, endothelial function, and post-prandial glycemia. That multi-component effect is why its relationship to Cardiovascular disease tends to be more consistent than any single food inside the pattern.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link mediterranean diet pattern to lower risk of cardiovascular disease in general adult. The average effect is usually moderate rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
